The longest river in the world is the Nile River.

In the provided text, the central conflict is a moral and cultural clash between individual greed and collective heritage. Jacob, a prospector, faces the challenge of balancing his personal desire for wealth against the sacred rights and traditions of the indigenous tribe. This internal struggle is exacerbated by external pressures, as the discovery attracts outsiders, forcing Jacob to make a critical decision about where his true loyalties lie—whether with his own economic gain or with respecting the land and people he has encountered.
